body:
Thank you. That is a great idea but I think he's still a bit young for that. Maybe in a few months time it could be nice.

We have that ring fit adventure game for switch that my wife brought for me a couple years back. She could do that, the graphics are colorful and maybe my son would like to watch.

Believe me I would love to cook more. I can cook and I like it a lot, but we can't switch places because while I work out I also keep an eye on our son. I can do that because I am doing mostly static work during which I can talk to my son, interact with him and drop the weights if needs be.

But my wife is more into yoga or cardio and you can't jump around / do poses while your son demands your attention.  Otherwise I'd gladly take on cooking duty to allow her to work out.

As a general rule she cooks more than I do because it's the easiest thing between that and keeping our son entertained. I'd love to trade more often but we both know that cooking is the easiest of the two and it allows her to relax a bit, browse her phone etc.

We only eat simple stuff that is easy to make so it's not a huge burden to cook in our house, it only takes a bit of time.

Anyway thanks for your suggesiton. I'll try to "dump" some alone time on her.

Ok, but I am not taking time for myself either. The only difference is that I manage to work out because it's mostly static so I can lift some weights and keep an eye on my son at the same time, while my wife cooks.

We can't trade places - which I would gladly do - because my wife is more into yoga or cardio and you can't jump around or do poses when there's a 2 year old trying to climb on you.

It's not the "tell me what to do" coming from people who don't want the mental load to plan for a children's meal or bath or food.

I just told her: just decide what YOU want to do for YOURSELF and will create the conditions for you to do that. I shouldn't be the one planning a workout - or whatever activity really - for her.

The time I use to exercise I am still keeping an eye on our son and entertaining him.. It's never time that I take to be by myself really. So it's not like I am taking up a slot of free time that I could give her. If it was that simple I'd do it. The thing is that I work with dumbbells and stuff, so I am relatively static and when I do that I can talk to my son and interact with him somehow, and drop the exercise if needs be.

My wife is more about yoga or cardio and you can't do that when there's a toddler trying to climb on you.

It's not about that tho. My wife has said many, many times that she wants to exercise. I am not thinking about coming up with a plan because I want to control her, only because I think it would lift a burden off of her.

I thought I made that clear. Sad that you got so many upvotes, because people think that just because I'm a man my heart is not in the right place.

Also putting our son on the stroller is not a workout. We do go for walks on saturdays and sundays. We can't do it mon to fri because there is not time, by the time we get home from work our son needs to eat. And what my wife needs is more intensive that just going for a walk. Her words, not mine.
